headline: The supported Node.js floor is 26.13.1, trusted keep-alive origins apply to caller agents and change without dropping transfers, and an HTTP/2 stream that closes early fails at once
summary:
The `engines.node` floor is `>=26.13.1`, the Node.js release that fixes the November 2026 HTTP/2, HTTPS and TLS vulnerabilities. Node 24 is no longer supported. `b.security.assertProduction()` reports `security/node-version` below Node 26 and `security/node-patch-level` on a release without those fixes, and names each missing CVE.

`b.httpClient.configurePool({ trustedKeepAliveOrigins })` no longer destroys pooled connections: requests in flight finish, and only idle connections of an origin removed from the list close. The list now also applies to an agent passed in `opts.agent`, so a mutual-TLS client built with `b.pqcAgent.create({ cert, key })` reuses its connections to a trusted origin.

An HTTP/2 stream that closes before its response headers arrive rejects with `http-client/h2-stream-error` instead of waiting for `timeoutMs`, and a stream whose session closes mid-body rejects with the transient `http-client/truncated-body`. The vendored `@blamejs/pki` is 0.9.13 and the Public Suffix List is refreshed.

items.title: Node.js 26.13.1 is the supported floor
items.body: `engines.node` in `package.json` is `>=26.13.1`. Node 26.13.1 fixes CVE-2026-123863, CVE-2026-123865, CVE-2026-123866 and CVE-2026-123868 in the HTTP/2 server, CVE-2026-123864 in the HTTPS server, and CVE-2026-123872 and CVE-2026-126051 in TLS, and bundles OpenSSL 3.5.9. `b.security.assertProduction()` defaults `minNodeMajor` to 26 and reports `security/node-version` on Node 24 and earlier. Its `security/node-patch-level` check fails on a Node release that lacks any of those fixes or the Brotli decoder fix (CVE-2026-111497), lists the missing CVEs, and advises upgrading to Node 26.13.1 or later. A prerelease build such as `26.13.1-pre` and every 23.x and 25.x release are treated as unfixed. An operator who sets `minNodeMajor: 24` is held to 24.22.3, the 24.x release with the same fixes. Upgrade with your Node.js installer or base image before upgrading the framework.

items.title: The wiki container builds on Node 26.13.1
items.body: `examples/wiki/Dockerfile` pins Chainguard `node:latest-dev` and `node:latest` digests that carry Node 26.13.1 and OpenSSL 4.0.3. A local `docker build` with no build arguments now passes the framework's Node and OpenSSL patch-floor check inside the image.

items.title: `configurePool({ trustedKeepAliveOrigins })` keeps transfers in flight (#891)
items.body: A call that sets only `trustedKeepAliveOrigins` keeps every transport and connection. The client reads the list when each response ends, so a change applies to connections already open: idle connections of an origin removed from the list close at once, and its connections in flight close when their responses end. A call that sets an agent option or `certificateCompression` retires the transport cache instead of destroying it: idle connections close, a request in flight finishes on the connection it started on, and later requests open new transports with the new values. Before this release every call destroyed all pooled HTTP/1.1 sockets and HTTP/2 sessions, which aborted requests and streamed downloads on every origin.

items.title: `trustedKeepAliveOrigins` applies to an agent passed in `opts.agent` (#892)
items.body: An https request through an agent passed to `b.httpClient.request` in `opts.agent`, such as a `b.pqcAgent.create({ cert, key, ca })` agent for mutual TLS, keeps its connection open after the response ends and reuses it for a later request to the same origin when the origin is listed in `trustedKeepAliveOrigins` and the agent's own `keepAlive` allows it. The client marks the agent on first use. A request that other code sends through the same agent still gets its own connection, and a `b.network.proxy` agent never reuses a TLS connection.

items.title: An HTTP/2 stream that closes early fails without waiting for the timeout
items.body: `b.httpClient.request` rejects with `http-client/h2-stream-error` when an HTTP/2 stream closes before its response headers arrive, and includes the stream's reset code when there is one. Before this release the request waited for `timeoutMs`. A buffered or streamed HTTP/2 body whose session closes before the stream ends rejects with `http-client/truncated-body`, marked transient so `b.retry.isRetryable` returns true. Before this release such a body could resolve as complete.

items.title: Vendored `@blamejs/pki` 0.9.13 and the Public Suffix List
items.body: `lib/vendor/blamejs-pki.cjs` is `@blamejs/pki` 0.9.13, refreshed with `scripts/vendor-update.sh`; the upstream change from 0.9.12 is documentation and its `engines` field. The vendored Public Suffix List is the 2026-11-20 snapshot. `lib/vendor/MANIFEST.json` and `NOTICE` carry the new versions and hashes.

items.title: ML-KEM and ML-DSA keys written on Node 24 load on Node 26
items.body: SECURITY.md "Node 26 compatibility" lists the measured PKCS8 sizes: Node 24.21 and earlier write the seed and the expanded key (3266 bytes for ML-KEM-1024, 4098 for ML-DSA-65, 4962 for ML-DSA-87), and Node 24.22.0 and later and Node 26 write the seed alone (86 bytes for ML-KEM, 54 for ML-DSA). Node 26 imports both, and refuses a blob whose seed and expanded key disagree with `ERR_OSSL_INVALID_KEY`. A vault key, a sealed value and audit-sign keys that blamejs wrote on Node 24.21 load and verify through `b.vault` and `b.auditSign` on Node 26; no key migration is needed.

items.title: `localDb.thin` names the supported Node release
items.body: When `node:sqlite` is unavailable, `localdb-thin/sqlite-missing` reads `requires Node 26.13.1 or later`.

items.title: Hand-rolled get-or-insert on a `Map`
items.body: The codebase-patterns gate fails on a `has` then `set`, a `get` falsy or `undefined` check then `set`, a memoizing `has`/`get` return followed by `set`, and a `get(key) || default` followed by `set`, each with or without braces. A site whose control flow depends on the key being absent carries an `allow:keyed-insert-absence-drives` marker with its reason.
